title: Child-Pugh Score
sources: Pugh RN, Murray-Lyon IM, Dawson JL, et al. Transection of the oesophagus for bleeding oesophageal varices. Br J Surg. 1973;60(8):646-649.
Child CG, Turcotte JG. Surgery and portal hypertension. In: The Liver and Portal Hypertension. 1964.

changelog.change: Initial entry — a genuine content gap (MELD-Na existed but its long-standing bedside companion, still widely used for surgical-risk and prognosis conversations, did not).

purpose: Grades cirrhosis severity from labs plus two clinical exam findings (ascites, encephalopathy) — older and less precise than MELD-Na for transplant allocation, but still the standard reference for surgical-risk stratification and the classic A/B/C prognostic classes.

interpretation.label: Class B
interpretation.risk: Significant functional compromise — ~80% 1-year survival; elevated perioperative risk, especially for major surgery

interpretation.label: Class C
interpretation.risk: Decompensated — ~45% 1-year survival; elective surgery is generally avoided, and even necessary procedures carry substantial risk

notes: For transplant listing and organ allocation, MELD-Na is the current standard (see meld-na) — Child-Pugh's continued relevance is mainly perioperative risk stratification (a Class C patient is a very different surgical conversation than a Class A) and as a quick prognostic anchor that doesn't require a calculator app to eyeball at the bedside.
buildNote: Standard additive engine — the one score in this codebase where each item's point range starts at 1 rather than 0, matching the original 1-3 per-parameter scale exactly.
